experiment: Re-check rate after wrong vs right non-final candidate answers in RL's T2 texts, as a ratio
recipe: File: s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (all 500 rows, cap hits included). Field text. Candidates, in text order: (a) each '\boxed{' with brace-balanced content (candidate string = content; skip if unbalanced before end of text; end = index after the matching '}'); (b) each match of the case-insensitive regex 'answer is:?\s*' followed by the span up to the first newline, '. ' or end of text (candidate string = that span with '$', '\(', '\)', '*' and a trailing '.' removed); (c) each line matching '^\s*\**Answer:?\**\s*(.+)$' (candidate = group 1, cleaned as in b). A box inside a (b)/(c) span counts once, as the box. Grade each candidate right iff the equivalence function of grader/rln4_grader_v3.py (the one behind score_v3) judges it equal to the row's gold; empty strings are wrong. Keep only non-final candidates: at least 800 characters of text follow the candidate's end. Re-check flag = the case-insensitive regex '\b(wait|hmm|let me (double[- ]?)?check|let me verify|double[- ]?check)\b' matches in the 800 characters after the candidate's end. Pool candidates over rows. r_W = flagged/total among wrong candidates, r_R = same among right candidates. Statistic = r_W / r_R. Report it even if there are few wrong candidates.

experiment: Difference-in-differences of re-check rates, RL (T2) minus base (T1), wrong minus right non-final candidates
recipe: Apply the candidate extraction, grading, non-final filter and re-check flag of prediction 1 to s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL) and to s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base + cue), all 500 rows each, cap hits included. For each file compute r_W and r_R (pooled over rows). Statistic D = (r_W(T2) - r_W(T1)) - (r_R(T2) - r_R(T1)). If a file has zero non-final candidates in a class, that rate is 0.

experiment: Share of final-right answers containing a right non-final candidate followed by a re-check: RL minus base
recipe: Files: s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL) and s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base + cue). Recompute each row's final score with grader/rln4_grader_v3.py (the score_v3 procedure). Keep rows whose final score is right and that are not cap hits (cap_hit false). For each kept row, use the candidate extraction, grading, non-final filter and re-check flag of prediction 1. The row counts 1 if it has at least one right non-final candidate with the re-check flag set, else 0. F(file) = mean over kept rows. Statistic = F(T2) - F(T1).

experiment: First-marker regrade of the base's wrong T1 answers: among T1 rows graded wrong by grader v3 on the full text, the fraction whose first answer marker is right.
recipe: File: s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (500 rows, base + cue, T 1.0). For each row, v3_last = grader/rln4_grader_v3.py applied to the full text against gold (recomputed, since the record has no v3 column). First marker = whichever of these starts earliest in text: (a) a line whose left-stripped text begins with 'Answer:', with content = the rest of that line; (b) the first '\boxed{', with content = the brace-balanced contents. first_score = grader v3 applied to the string 'Answer: ' + content against gold. A row with no marker gets first_score 0. Filter: rows with v3_last == 0, cap hits included. Statistic: (rows with first_score == 1) / (rows with v3_last == 0).

experiment: Direction of first/last disagreement on T1: among rows where the first-marker grade differs from the last-marker grade, the share that are first-right and last-wrong.
recipe: File: s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl, all 500 rows, cap hits included. v3_last and first_score are defined exactly as in the previous recipe (first marker = earliest 'Answer:' line or '\boxed{'; no marker gives first_score 0). Discordant rows: first_score != v3_last. Statistic: (discordant rows with first_score == 1) / (discordant rows). If there are no discordant rows, the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Net first-marker gain for the base on the four Day-1 #3 samples: (first-marker right count minus stored v3 right count) over all attempt-0 rows.
recipe: File: iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153825-208b/answers.jsonl (base + cue, T 1.0, 4 samples). Filter: attempt == 0 (500 problems x 4 samples = 2,000 rows; missing rows are dropped and the denominator is the number of rows present). v3_last = the stored score_v3. first_score as in the first recipe (earliest 'Answer:' line or '\boxed{' content, graded by grader/rln4_grader_v3.py as 'Answer: ' + content; no marker gives 0; cap hits included). Statistic: (sum of first_score - sum of v3_last) / number of rows.

experiment: The same net first-marker gain for the RL model on its four Day-1 #3 samples.
recipe: File: iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-183640-e828/answers.jsonl (RL plain, T 1.0, 4 samples). Filter: attempt == 0 (missing rows are dropped and the denominator is the number of rows present). v3_last = the stored score_v3. first_score as in the first recipe (earliest 'Answer:' line or '\boxed{' content, graded by grader/rln4_grader_v3.py as 'Answer: ' + content; no marker gives 0; cap hits included). Statistic: (sum of first_score - sum of v3_last) / number of rows.

experiment: Wrong rate among base answers that keep going and state a new answer after the first one: among finished T1 answers with more than 300 characters and at least one further marker after the first marker, the fraction graded wrong by v3.
recipe: File: s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl. Filter: cap_hit false and at least one marker (first marker defined as in the first recipe). End of first marker: for an 'Answer:' line, the end of that line (or the end of text); for '\boxed{', the position just after its matching closing brace. Keep rows where the text after that end is longer than 300 characters AND contains another 'Answer:' line (a left-stripped line beginning 'Answer:') or another '\boxed{'. Statistic: (kept rows with v3_last == 0) / (kept rows), with v3_last recomputed by grader/rln4_grader_v3.py. If no rows are kept, the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Numeric-equivalence recovery rate of the cued base's finished, v3-wrong answers on non-integer-gold hard328 problems.
recipe: File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (run_cell rows; fields problem_index, gold, extracted, extracted_v3, score_v3, cap_hit). Normalisation N(s): if s is entirely \boxed{...}, take the inside; remove '$', all whitespace, '\left', '\right', '\displaystyle', '\,', '\!', '\;', '^\circ', '^{\circ}'; replace '\dfrac' and '\tfrac' with '\frac'; drop one trailing '.'; if the result contains '=' and none of '<', '>', '\le', '\ge', take the part after the last '='. A gold counts as an integer if N(gold) matches ^-?\d+$; otherwise it is non-integer. Equivalence E(a, g): false if either string is empty, or either N-string contains ',' or '\cup' (tuples, sets, intervals). Otherwise parse N(a) and N(g) with sympy.parsing.latex.parse_latex. It is false on any parse error, on unequal free-symbol sets, or on a timeout of 5 s per pair. With no free symbols, compare the evaluated values. With symbols, substitute 5 points (numpy default_rng(0), each symbol uniform on [0.5, 2.5], the same points for both). True iff every evaluation is finite and real and |a - g| <= 1e-6 * max(1, |g|). Denominator: rows with non-integer gold, score_v3 == 0, cap_hit false, and at least one of extracted_v3 or extracted non-empty. Numerator: those rows where E(extracted_v3, gold) or E(extracted, gold) is true. Report numerator / denominator. Cap-hit rows are excluded. Ties do not arise (one row per problem). Missing rows are excluded from both counts.

experiment: The same numeric-equivalence recovery rate for RL's finished, v3-wrong answers on non-integer-gold hard328 problems.
recipe: File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL plain). Use exactly the N, integer-gold test, E, denominator and numerator of the previous recipe: rows with non-integer gold, score_v3 == 0, cap_hit false, and extracted_v3 or extracted non-empty. A row is recovered if E(extracted_v3, gold) or E(extracted, gold) is true. Report recovered / denominator. Cap-hit rows are excluded and missing rows are excluded.

experiment: Exact-string match to gold among answers that v3 grades right, RL minus base, on non-integer-gold problems that both models got right.
recipe: Files: the e72c (base cue) and 86ef (RL plain) answers.jsonl named above. Join on problem_index. Keep the problems where N(gold) is non-integer (N and the integer test as in the first recipe) and score_v3 == 1 in both files. For each model, the indicator is 1 iff N(extracted_v3) == N(gold) as strings. Statistic: (mean indicator for 86ef) minus (mean indicator for e72c) over the kept problems. A problem missing from either file is dropped. An empty extracted_v3 counts as 0.

experiment: The hard328 gap, RL plain minus base cue, after both are regraded with v3 OR numeric equivalence.
recipe: Files: the e72c and 86ef answers.jsonl named above. For every row, regraded = 1 if score_v3 == 1, or if cap_hit is false and E(extracted_v3, gold) or E(extracted, gold) is true (E and N as in the first recipe, applied to all golds, integer or not). Otherwise regraded = 0. A cap-hit row keeps its score_v3. A problem_index of the 328 clean problems that is missing from a file counts as 0. Statistic: 100 * (sum of regraded over 86ef - sum of regraded over e72c) / 328, in points.

experiment: Base+cue, Levels 1-3: median over problems of the within-problem log length ratio of finished-wrong samples to their right siblings.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json (key problems; fields index, level, base_k). Keep rows with attempt == 0 (samples 0-3). Keep problems in pool_k_le3 with base_k in {1,2,3} and level in {1,2,3}. Per row: right = score_v3 == 1; finished-wrong = cap_hit false and score_v3 == 0; cap-hit rows are dropped entirely (neither right nor wrong). For each kept problem with at least one finished-wrong row and at least one right row: m = median n_new of its right rows; for each finished-wrong row r_i = ln(n_new_i / m); problem value = mean of its r_i. Problems lacking a right or a finished-wrong attempt-0 row, or missing from rows.jsonl, are excluded. Statistic = median of the problem values (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values).

experiment: Base+cue, Level 5: the same within-problem log length ratio.
recipe: Same files, filters and computation as the Levels 1-3 statistic (attempt == 0; base_k in {1,2,3} from pool_k_le3.json; right = score_v3 == 1; finished-wrong = cap_hit false and score_v3 == 0; cap hits dropped; per problem the mean over its finished-wrong rows of ln(n_new / median n_new of its right rows); problems lacking either kind excluded), but keep only problems with level == 5. Statistic = median of the problem values.

experiment: Mechanism test, base+cue Levels 1-3: the share of finished-wrong samples shorter than every right sibling. The nearest rival (slips accumulate with length, r3-surprises-1) puts wrong samples on the long side, giving about 0.2 or less (below the ~0.3 a length-blind null gives for 1-3 right siblings); premature commitment gives well above chance.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json. Keep rows with attempt == 0; problems with base_k in {1,2,3} and level in {1,2,3}. Right = score_v3 == 1; finished-wrong = cap_hit false and score_v3 == 0; cap-hit rows dropped. Over all finished-wrong rows (pooled across problems) whose problem has at least one right attempt-0 row: count a row as a hit if its n_new is strictly less than the n_new of every right row of the same problem (a tie with any right row is not a hit). Statistic = hits / number of such finished-wrong rows.

experiment: RL plain, all levels: the within-problem log length ratio of finished-wrong to right siblings.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json (fields index, level, rl_k). Keep rows with attempt == 0; keep problems in pool_k_le3 with rl_k in {1,2,3}, any level. Right = score_v3 == 1; finished-wrong = cap_hit false and score_v3 == 0; cap-hit rows dropped. For each problem with at least one finished-wrong and one right row: problem value = mean over its finished-wrong rows of ln(n_new / median n_new of its right rows). Problems lacking either kind excluded. Statistic = median of problem values.

experiment: Per-problem log length ratio of top8 plain to the cued base, ln(top8 n_generated / T1 tokens), taken as the median over problems. This tests the mechanism. This theory says top8 has the cued base's length, so the median is near 0 (slightly positive if top8 has fewer cap hits). The nearest rival (knowledge-69adda / r1-surprises-2: recovering arms take RL's length) says top8 has RL's length. It predicts the same statistic computed with t2_generated_tokens in place of top8, about 0.6.
recipe: Load studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/top8_plain-01/per_problem.json and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Join on problem_index and keep the problems present in both (drop missing rows). For each problem compute ln(max(n_generated,1) / max(t1_generated_tokens,1)), with n_generated from the top8 file. Keep cap hits, at their stored token counts. Report the median over the joined problems. If the count is even, the median is the mean of the two middle values.

experiment: Count of quick finished-wrong answers in top8 plain: answers wrong under v3, not cap hits, and at most 2,000 generated tokens. This tests whether the edit carries RL's checking policy. This theory (base-type errors without RL's checking) predicts about the cued base's count (T1 has 13 wrong among its 263 answers of <= 2,000 tokens). The RL-checking rival predicts 0-3 (RL has 0 wrong among answers of <= 4,000 tokens). The partial-dose rival predicts about 5.
recipe: Load studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/top8_plain-01/per_problem.json. Count the rows with score_v3 == 0, cap_hit false and n_generated <= 2000. Rows with a missing score_v3 are left out. Each problem_index counts once.

experiment: Fraction of the cued base's wrong problems (T1 wrong) that top8 plain also gets wrong.
recipe: Join studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json with studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/top8_plain-01/per_problem.json on problem_index. Keep the problems with t1_right false (a T1 cap hit counts as wrong) that are present in both files. Report the fraction of those whose top8 score_v3 == 0. A top8 cap hit counts as wrong. Problems missing from the top8 file are dropped.

experiment: Count of Think-SFT cue answers that hit the 16,384 cap on MATH-500.
recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json. Count rows with cap_hit true, one row per problem_index (if a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order). Missing problems (of indices 0-499) count as not cap hits. Report the integer count.

experiment: Mechanism test: share of Think-SFT's wrong answers that are cap hits. The nearest rival (Think-SFT as a uniformly stronger solver on the base's difficulty axis) predicts about the cued base's own share, roughly 0.30 (27 cap hits among about 90 wrong); this theory predicts most wrong answers are cap hits.
recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json, one row per problem_index (first row in file order if repeated). Wrong = score_v3 equal to 0 (or missing or null). Statistic = (number of wrong rows with cap_hit true) / (number of wrong rows). Problems absent from the file are left out of both counts. Report as a fraction.

experiment: Share of Think-SFT cap hits that fall in the top quartile of RL's answer length on MATH-500. Random placement gives 0.25.
recipe: Files studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json and studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json, joined on problem_index. Sort the 500 problems by t2_generated_tokens ascending, ties broken by problem_index ascending; Q4 = ranks 376-500. Statistic = (Think-SFT rows with cap_hit true whose problem is in Q4) / (all Think-SFT rows with cap_hit true). Problems missing from either file are dropped. Report as a fraction.

experiment: Where Think-SFT's deficit to RL lies: Think-SFT right minus RL (T2) right within the top RL-length quartile.
recipe: Same join and quartiles as the previous recipe (sort by t2_generated_tokens ascending, ties by problem_index, Q4 = ranks 376-500). Within Q4 compute (number of problems with Think-SFT score_v3 = 1) minus (number with t2_right true). A missing or null Think-SFT score counts as 0. Report the signed integer.

experiment: Mean generated tokens per problem of Think-SFT cue on MATH-500, against RL plain's 4,694 at the same setting.
recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json, one row per problem_index (first row if repeated). Statistic = arithmetic mean of n_generated over all rows, cap hits included at their stored n_generated. Rows with missing n_generated are dropped. Report in tokens.

experiment: Per-hold-on revision rate, base vs RL, on stored MATH-500 text: the fraction of hold-on occurrences where the first number after the token differs from the last number before it (re-derive) rather than equals it (restate). Reported as base rate / RL rate. The rival r4-m06 (constant hold-on bias, re-checks at the base's rate) predicts about 1.0 (0.9 to 1.1).
recipe: Files: S3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base, cue) and r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL, plain), MATH-500 n=500. Use rows with cap_hit false only; skip missing rows. In each row's text, delete commas between digits (regex (?<=\d),(?=\d{3}) replaced by ''). Hold-on occurrence = each match of the case-sensitive regex (?<![A-Za-z])(Wait|Hmm)(?![A-Za-z]). Number = each match of \d+(?:\.\d+)?, compared as exact strings. For an occurrence with match start s and end e: before = text[max(0,s-300):s], after = text[e:e+400]. The occurrence is eligible only if before and after each contain at least one number. It is a revision if the last number in before differs from the first number in after. Per model, pool all eligible occurrences over all finished answers, right and wrong: rate = revisions / eligible. Statistic = base rate / RL rate. No grading is needed.
unit: ratio of per-occurrence revision rates (base / RL)

experiment: Among the base's finished-wrong MATH-500 answers that contain at least one hold-on, the fraction whose final answer was already written before the last hold-on.
recipe: Files: S3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl joined by problem_index to studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Keep rows with cap_hit false (row field) and t1_right false (grader v3, per_problem.json). Hold-on regex as in the first prediction, on text; keep rows with at least one match, and let s_last be the start of the last match. Final answer = extracted_v2 if non-empty, else extracted (v1); drop the row if both are empty. Normalize the answer: strip whitespace, remove every '$', and if it is wrapped in \boxed{...}, take the inside. Kept = the normalized answer occurs in text[:s_last] (with commas between digits deleted, as above, on both strings) at a position where the character just before and the character just after are not letters or digits (string boundaries count as such). Statistic = kept rows / kept-plus-not-kept rows. Missing rows and cap hits are excluded.

experiment: Detection parity in generated text on hard-328: how much denser hold-ons are in wrong finished answers than in right ones, base relative to RL. This theory (equal detection) predicts about 1. The better-detector rival r2-revise-2 (RL d' 1.1 vs base 0.6) predicts below 0.7.
recipe: Files: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base, cue) and r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL, plain), clean 328, T 1.0. Use rows with cap_hit false; right = score_v3 == 1, wrong = otherwise. Rows with empty text count with density 0. Density of a row = number of matches of the hold-on regex of the first prediction / (len(text) / 1000). For each model, R = (mean density over finished-wrong rows) / (mean density over finished-right rows). Statistic = R_base / R_RL. If a model has no finished-wrong rows or a right-row mean of 0, report as undefined (counts as refuted).
unit: ratio of wrong/right hold-on density ratios (base / RL)

experiment: Pool fresh base samples with seeds independent of Day-1 #3 sample 0 and count how many of the 17 RL-solved base-0/4 problems get at least one right answer.
recipe: Problems: entries of studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json key `problems` with base_k == 0 and rl_k >= 1. Pool per problem (index = problem_index): (a) studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl rows with attempt in {1, 2}, score_v3; (b) studies/rlneurons/results/axis/math500-01/vectors.json, the arm whose manifest.json job id is abaybektursun-1114-153047-6429 (random matched-norm difference, cue), its 0/1 at the problem's position in problem_indices; (c) the same file, the arm with job id abaybektursun-1114-183855-e840 (base-written examples), absent for problems not in its problem_indices; (d) iterate-runs:frustea-1114-180853-e383/answers.jsonl rows with attempt 0 (or no attempt field), score_v3; (e) s3 r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl, every row (all samples), with v3 recomputed by grader/rln4_grader_v3.py from text and gold; (f) studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/screen100/base_cue-01/per_problem.json score_v3 (problems 0-99 only). Leave out every other source. A problem counts as solved if any pooled sample has v3 score 1. Cap hits count as wrong (their score as stored or recomputed); a missing source or row adds nothing. Statistic: solved problems / 17.

experiment: Mechanism test against the dose-scaling / new-solution rival: the pooled solve fraction on the 17 RL-solved base-0/4 problems minus the same fraction on the 16 base-0/4 problems RL never solves. The rival (RL creates paths where the base's p is about 0) predicts a difference of about 0.00; this theory predicts a clearly positive one.
recipe: Use the pool, solve rule, cap-hit and missing-row rules of the first prediction. A = solved / 17 over pool_k_le3.json problems with base_k == 0 and rl_k >= 1; B = solved / 16 over problems with base_k == 0 and rl_k == 0. Statistic: A - B (if the class sizes differ from 17 / 16, divide by the actual class sizes).

experiment: Per-sample base success rate in the independent pool on the 17 RL-solved base-0/4 problems: the mechanism says 'a few percent' per sample, not about 0 and not near the base's overall 0.82.
recipe: Same 17 problems and the same sources (a)-(f) as the first prediction. Each pooled row or arm entry present for the problem is one sample (a vectors.json arm entry is 1 sample; F_math500 rows count one per row). Statistic: total samples with v3 score 1 / total samples present, summed over the 17 problems (a pooled ratio, not a mean of per-problem rates). Cap hits count as wrong samples; missing sources add no samples.

experiment: Share of step-100 plain MATH-500 answers at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 that open with the RL cue's first token 'line'. The sharpening rival (r4-m10) and the length rival leave the opening as the plain base's, near 0.
recipe: Fetch s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (aws s3 cp ... --profile iterate-ecr). Keep rows with sample == 0. If a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. For each row, test whether text.lstrip() starts with the 4 characters 'line' (case-sensitive). Statistic: the number of rows that pass divided by the number of kept rows. Cap-hit rows count like any other row. Problems with no row are left out of the denominator.

experiment: Mechanism test: within the step-100 plain T 0.6 answers, the cap-hit rate of answers that open with 'line' minus the cap-hit rate of answers that do not. This mechanism expects about the cued-base minus plain-base gap (0.24 - 0.13 = 0.11). The nearest rival, policy sharpening that crosses top-p's lock threshold (r4-m10), raises cap hits whatever the opening and expects about 0.00. The length-growth rival also expects about 0.00.
recipe: Same file and filters as prediction 1 (s0100/P_math500.jsonl, sample == 0, first row per problem_index). Group A: rows where text.lstrip() starts with 'line'. Group B: all other kept rows. For each group, cap-hit rate = number of rows with cap_hit true divided by the group's row count. Statistic: rate(A) - rate(B). If either group has fewer than 20 rows, the prediction counts as refuted. Missing problems are left out.

experiment: Mechanism test on the plain base itself: in base-01's plain MATH-500 answers at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, the cap-hit rate of answers that open in the cue's register ('Okay' within the first 12 characters, e.g. '.\n\nOkay') minus the rate of the other answers. This mechanism says the register drives the loops and expects a clearly positive gap. A rival in which loops depend only on problem length or difficulty and not on the opening expects about 0.
recipe: Fetch s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (aws s3 cp ... --profile iterate-ecr). Keep rows with sample == 0 and the first row per problem_index. Group A: rows where the substring 'Okay' occurs in text[:12]. Group B: all other kept rows. For each group, cap-hit rate = number of rows with cap_hit true divided by the group's row count. Statistic: rate(A) - rate(B). If either group has fewer than 20 rows, the prediction counts as refuted. Missing problems are left out.

experiment: Share of step-100's finished plain T 0.6 answers that still state the result on an 'Answer:' line (the base's format). This mechanism expects a base-like share. A format-shift rival, in which early RL already moves the policy to RL's boxed format (RL share 0.00), expects near 0.
recipe: Same file and filters as prediction 1 (s0100/P_math500.jsonl, sample == 0, first row per problem_index). Keep only rows with cap_hit false. A row counts if any line of text, after str.lstrip(), starts with 'Answer:' (case-sensitive), where lines are text.split('\n'). Statistic: rows that count divided by finished rows. experiment: Share of Code 3.1's lead over Code 3.0 (MATH-500, cue, T 1.0) that lies in the top quartile of RL answer length. The nearest rival (Code 3.0 is a base-like model lacking math transfer, distributed like the base-vs-RL gap) predicts about 0.35; this mechanism predicts 0.62.
